messages:
Sam: quick follow-up to the offload allocator RFC — small-page thresholds and allocator boundaries. want to lock down defaults and the minimal API for hinting/pinning before the next canary. anyone got fresh perf or design objections?

Anya: main practical worry: CPU-side fragmentation after lots of short-lived tensors (chat workloads). small pages reduce internal waste but increase external frag. my gut: 32KB threshold for 'small' pages + per-thread freelist for hot sizes. also prefer explicit compaction trigger instead of automatic background compaction (:thinking:).

Lee: ran microbench yesterday on the emulation cluster. summary:
- 32KB threshold -> 95% drop in page churn for small-seq workloads (batch <= 8)
- but external fragmentation went up ~7% on long-running 2048-token runs (lots of different sizes)
- enabling a lightweight slab for powers-of-two up to 256KB cut fragmentation back down while keeping churn low.

Riley: API thought: expose a hint to the runtime on allocate so callers can say `hint=ephemeral|pinned|kvcache`. sketch:
```
Allocator.allocate(size, hint="ephemeral")
# hint affects: pin vs pageable, preferred pool, async-copy behavior
Allocator.compact(range)  # on-demand compaction/migration
```
we can keep current Allocate/Free shape and add an opt-in interface to avoid breaking customers.

Anya: +1 for opt-in. also: defaults must be tuned for hosted vs dedicated. hosted should favor lower latency (more pinning) whereas dedicated can be more cost-sensitive. recommend feature flag `offload.compaction.enabled` and `offload.small_page_threshold`.

offload-bot: Canary: offload-allocator-v2 deployed to canary cluster (canary-12). Observability hooks instrumented: offload.page_churn, offload.compaction_cycles, allocator.external_frag_bytes.

Sam: perfect — metrics listed by bot are exactly what we need. can we agree to: default small_page_threshold = 32KB, slab up to 256KB, buddy allocator above that, expose `hint` arg, and compaction as an opt-in API/flag?

Lee: i can live with 32KB default. i'll add the slab+buddies implementation to my branch and run long seq tests through the perf harness (24h run) to catch slow drift.

Riley: will open a small RFC PR for the allocator API (backwards compatible) and include the config snippet + migration doc. one question: how do we handle pinned host memory vs cudaMallocManaged for offload? proposal: prefer pinned host pages for async copy when hint=pinned; fallback to pageable with synchronous copy for legacy callers.

Anya: agree. also add a watchdog that triggers compaction if `offload.page_churn > X` for Y minutes — but make it disabled in Dedicated by default. we don't want surprise CPU spikes.

Sam: action items:
- @Lee: land slab+buddies perf branch and run long-run tests (start 1769010000)
- @Riley: RFC PR for Allocator.hints + compaction API
- @Anya: write a short doc on config flags and recommended defaults for Hosted vs Dedicated
- @Sam: add dashboard panels for the three metrics and an alert template for high external_frag_bytes

Riley: quick config example for the PR: 
```
# offload.conf
small_page_threshold = 32KB
slab_max = 256KB
use_hugepages = false
pinned_threshold = 1MB
async_copy = true
compaction_enabled = false  # opt-in
```

Sam: nice. let's keep the RFC light and ship the config behind a feature flag. thanks everyone — follow-up PRs from @Lee and @Riley, doc from @Anya. if canary looks good we'll flip the flag for staging next week. :thumbsup:
